sentence: Centella asiatica (1_1_thankuni) is a Perennial Herb in the Apiaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical wetlands, marshy areas, tropical forests across Indian Subcontinent.
Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic brain tonic, memory enhancement, skin conditions, fever and contains active compounds like Asiaticoside, madecassoside, asiatic acid, madecassic acid.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical, 20-30°C, high humidity, 1500-2500mm rainfall annually and Loamy, well-drained, moist soil.
Safety considerations: Avoid high doses in pregnancy; minimal use acceptable in lactation under supervision.
Leaf features: Orbicular-reniform, 3-5cm across, crenate or sub-entire margins, glabrous, radiating nerves.
Bacopa monnieri (1_2_pathorkuchi) is a Perennial Herb (semi-aquatic) in the Plantaginaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical wetlands, marshes, pond margins, tropical monsoon forests across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic brain tonic, nerve tonic, cooling, digestive aid, skin conditions and contains active compounds like Bacosides (bacopaside I, II), bacosine, alkaloids (nicotine-like).
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-30°C, high humidity, 1200-2400mm rainfall and Sandy loam, well-drained moist soil, adaptable to aquatic conditions.
Safety considerations: Avoid in first trimester; minimal therapeutic use acceptable later under guidance.
Leaf features: Small, obovate to spoon-shaped, 4-6mm long, succulent, opposite arrangement.
Achyranthes aspera (1_3_apang) is a Annual/Biennial Herb in the Amaranthaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical dry forests, open grasslands, wastelands, disturbed areas across Indian Subcontinent, Africa.
Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic treatment for jaundice, urinary troubles, respiratory issues and contains active compounds like Saponins, alkaloids, essential oil, triterpenes.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 15-35°C, moderate rainfall, drought tolerant (800-1500mm) and Sandy loam, well-drained soil, tolerates poor soils.
Safety considerations: Avoid in pregnancy; safe in lactation at normal medicinal doses.
Leaf features: Lanceolate to elliptic, 2-5cm long, pubescent, margin entire, opposite arrangement.
Andrographis paniculata (1_4_kalomegh) is a Annual Herb (branched) in the Acanthaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical dry forests, cultivated fields, open grasslands across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic fever treatment, bitter tonic, liver support, digestive aid, wound healing and contains active compounds like Andrographolide (diterpenoid lactone), neoandrographolide, deoxyandrographolide.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-30°C, moderate rainfall (750-2250mm), prefers dry season and Well-drained loamy soil, slightly acidic to neutral pH.
Safety considerations: Avoid in pregnancy; minimal use acceptable in lactation.
Leaf features: Linear-lanceolate, 1-5cm long, glabrous, margin entire, opposite arrangement, acute apex.
Phyllanthus acidus (2_5_kaluchitra) is a Perennial Shrub/Small tree in the Phyllanthaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical deciduous forests, cultivated plantations, tropical wetlands across Tropical Asia, Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic cooling tonic, liver support, digestive aid, fever management, skin health and contains active compounds like Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), phyllanthin, hypophyllanthin, phyltetralin.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical, 20-32°C, moderate to high rainfall (1200-2400mm), humid conditions and Well-drained loamy soil, slightly acidic, fertile soil.
Safety considerations: Safe in pregnancy and lactation; traditionally used as nutritive tonic.
Leaf features: Leaflets small, 0.5-1.5cm, elliptic, feathery bipinnate arrangement, bright green.
Alternanthera sessilis (2_6_ayapan) is a Annual/Perennial Herb (prostrate spreading) in the Amaranthaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical wetlands, pond margins, marshes, disturbed areas across Indian Subcontinent, Southeast Asia.
Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic cooling herb, urinary support, fever reduction, liver support and contains active compounds like Alkaloids, saponins, phenols.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical, 20-30°C, high humidity, 1000-2500mm rainfall, moisture-loving and Moist loamy soil, adaptable to wet conditions.
Safety considerations: Avoid in pregnancy; minimal use in lactation.
Leaf features: Narrowly elliptic, 1-3cm long, glabrous, opposite arrangement, sessile.
Calotropis procera (2_7_akondo) is a Perennial Shrub/Small tree in the Apocynaceae family.
It naturally grows in Semi-arid regions, dry grasslands, waste areas, xerophytic habitats across Tropical Africa, Arabian Peninsula, Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Unani pain relief, traditional skin ulcer treatment, Ayurvedic wound care and contains active compounds like Cardenolides (cardiac glycosides), cardiac aglycones, alkaloids.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 15-40°C, drought resistant, 400-1200mm rainfall and Well-drained sandy soil, poor soil tolerance.
Safety considerations: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy; cardiotoxic potential.
Leaf features: Oblong-lanceolate, 6-12cm long, pubescent, waxy coating, opposite arrangement.
Desmodium triflorum (2_8_bamonhati) is a Perennial Herb (trailing) in the Fabaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical grasslands, forest edges, disturbed areas, cultivated fields across Tropical Asia, Indian Subcontinent.
Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic respiratory tonic, cough relief, asthma support, fever management and contains active compounds like Alkaloids, saponins, phenols, tannins.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical, 20-30°C, moderate rainfall (800-2000mm) and Well-drained sandy loam, adaptable soil.
Safety considerations: Generally safe in both pregnancy and lactation.
Leaf features: Trifoliate, leaflets 1-2cm, obovate, glabrous, opposite arrangement.
Amaranthus spinosus (3_9_kalodhutra) is a Annual Herb in the Amaranthaceae family.
It naturally grows in Open grasslands, disturbed areas, cultivated fields, waste areas across Tropical Americas, now pan-tropical.
Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic cooling tonic, digestive aid, urinary support, fever management and contains active compounds like Saponins, alkaloids, flavonoids.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-35°C, moderate rainfall (600-2000mm) and Well-drained soil, adaptable to poor soils.
Safety considerations: Safe; nutritive during pregnancy and lactation.
Leaf features: Broadly lanceolate, 3-7cm, glabrous, alternate arrangement, spines at leaf axils.
Scoparia dulcis (3_10_tarulata) is a Annual/Perennial Herb (compact shrub) in the Plantaginaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical grasslands, disturbed areas, cultivated fields, roadside across Tropical America, now pan-tropical.
Traditionally, it is used for Traditional fever remedy, urinary support, skin conditions, digestive aid and contains active compounds like Alkaloids, triterpenes, phenols.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical, 20-32°C, moderate rainfall (800-1800mm) and Well-drained soil, adaptable.
Safety considerations: Generally safe; minimal traditional restrictions.
Leaf features: Small, linear-lanceolate, 0.5-2cm, glabrous, whorled arrangement, margin entire.
Boerhavia diffusa (4_11_punarnava) is a Annual/Perennial Herb (prostrate spreading) in the Nyctaginaceae family.
It naturally grows in Open grasslands, disturbed areas, field margins, cultivated fields across Tropical Asia, Indian Subcontinent.
Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic diuretic and rejuvenative, kidney/urinary support, liver tonic, skin health and contains active compounds like Rotenone, alkaloids (boeravinone), flavonoids.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-35°C, moderate rainfall (600-2000mm) and Well-drained sandy loam, adaptable to poor soils.
Safety considerations: Avoid in pregnancy; minimal use in lactation.
Leaf features: Ovate, 1-3cm, glabrous to pubescent, slightly fleshy, opposite arrangement.
Justicia adhatoda (4_12_agnishikha) is a Perennial Shrub in the Acanthaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical deciduous forests, forest edges, cultivated areas across Indian Subcontinent, Southeast Asia.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic respiratory tonic, cough remedy, asthma support, tuberculosis support and contains active compounds like Vasicine (quinazoline alkaloid), vasicinone, essential oils.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-30°C, moderate rainfall (1000-2500mm) and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, slightly acidic.
Safety considerations: Avoid in pregnancy; safe in lactation.
Leaf features: Lanceolate, 8-15cm long, acuminate apex, pubescent, opposite arrangement.
Ocimum sanctum (4_13_tulsi) is a Annual/Short-lived perennial Herb (erect, branched) in the Lamiaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical regions, cultivated gardens, temple areas across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic adaptogen, stress relief, fever management, cough remedy, spiritual herb and contains active compounds like Eugenol, orientin, vicenin, rosmarinic acid, apigenin.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-28°C, moderate rainfall (1000-2000mm) and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, good drainage.
Safety considerations: Generally safe in pregnancy and lactation at normal culinary/mild therapeutic doses.
Leaf features: Ovate to oblong, 1-3cm, pubescent, margin serrate, opposite arrangement, aromatic.
Ocimum basilicum (4_14_ramtulshi) is a Annual Herb (erect, branched) in the Lamiaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical and subtropical regions, cultivated globally across Indian Subcontinent.
Traditionally, it is used for Culinary herb with medicinal properties, digestive aid, fever support and contains active compounds like Estragole, linalool, methyl cinnamate, eugenol (less than O.
sanctum).
Preferred cultivation conditions include Warm temperate to tropical, 18-28°C, moderate rainfall (500-1500mm) and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, good drainage.
Safety considerations: Safe in pregnancy and lactation at normal culinary amounts.
Leaf features: Ovate to oblong, 2-4cm, glabrous to pubescent, margin entire/serrate, opposite arrangement.
Adhatoda vasica (4_15_basok) is a Perennial Shrub in the Acanthaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical deciduous forests, forest margins, cultivated areas across Indian Subcontinent.
Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic cough remedy, respiratory support, asthma management, lung health and contains active compounds like Vasicine, vasicinone, alkaloids, essential oils.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-30°C, moderate rainfall (1000-2500mm) and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, slightly acidic.
Safety considerations: Avoid in pregnancy; safe in lactation.
Leaf features: Lanceolate, 10-18cm long, acuminate, pubescent, opposite arrangement.
Azadirachta indica (4_16_neem) is a Perennial (long-lived, 150-200+ years) Tree (medium) in the Meliaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical dry forests, deciduous forests, semi-arid regions across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic purifying herb, skin conditions, fever, parasites, liver support and contains active compounds like Azadirachtin (limonoid), nimbin, salannin, mahagoni, fatty acids.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 15-40°C, drought tolerant, 400-2250mm rainfall and Well-drained loamy soil, tolerates poor soils, slightly acidic to alkaline.
Safety considerations: AVOID seed oil in pregnancy (teratogenic potential); leaf use minimal and cautious.
Leaf features: Pinnate, leaflets lanceolate, 2-4cm, glabrous, serrate margin, feathery appearance.
Mentha piperita (4_17_pudina) is a Perennial Herb (stoloniferous, spreading) in the Lamiaceae family.
It naturally grows in Temperate to subtropical regions, cultivated globally across Hybrid species (Asia origin, Mediterranean cultivation).

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic cooling herb, digestive aid, headache relief, respiratory support and contains active compounds like Menthol (40-90%), menthone, limonene, pulegone, eucalyptol.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Temperate to subtropical, 10-28°C, moderate rainfall (500-1500mm), frost hardy and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, moist.
Safety considerations: Safe in pregnancy and lactation at normal culinary and mild therapeutic doses.
Leaf features: Lanceolate to elliptic, 2-4cm, glabrous, serrate margin, opposite arrangement, aromatic.
Hibiscus sabdariffa (4_18_joba) is a Annual/Perennial (depends on climate) Herb/Shrub in the Malvaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical grasslands, cultivated fields, open areas across Tropical Africa, Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic cooling tonic, blood pressure support, digestive aid, menstrual support and contains active compounds like Anthocyanins, flavonoids (hibiscetine), organic acids (citric, malic, tartaric).
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-32°C, moderate rainfall (750-2000mm) and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral.
Safety considerations: Generally safe at normal culinary amounts; avoid high medicinal doses in pregnancy.
Leaf features: Deeply lobed, 3-5 lobes, 5-10cm, serrate, glabrous to pubescent, alternate arrangement.
Moringa oleifera (4_19_sojina) is a Perennial Tree (small to medium) in the Moringaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical dry forests, semi-arid regions, cultivated widely across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic nutritive tonic, blood support, energy enhancement, skin health and contains active compounds like Proteins, amino acids, vitamins A/C, minerals, glucosinolates, niazimicin.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 15-35°C, drought tolerant, 400-2250mm rainfall and Well-drained sandy loam, tolerates poor soils, slightly alkaline to neutral.
Safety considerations: Leaves safe in pregnancy and lactation (nutritive); avoid root in pregnancy.
Leaf features: Tripinnate, leaflets small (0.3-0.8cm), ovate, glabrous, feathery appearance.
Ixora coccinea (5_20_gandha) is a Perennial Shrub in the Rubiaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical forests, cultivated gardens across South Asia, Indian Subcontinent.
Traditionally, it is used for Traditional skin conditions, wound healing, fever management, parasitic support and contains active compounds like Flavonoids, alkaloids, phenols, tannins.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-32°C, moderate to high rainfall (1000-2000mm) and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, slightly acidic.
Safety considerations: Generally safe.
Leaf features: Elliptic-oblong, 5-10cm, glabrous, opposite arrangement, leathery.
Polygonatum verticillatum (5_21_shotomuli) is a Perennial Herb (rhizomatous) in the Asparagaceae family.
It naturally grows in Temperate to subtropical forests, shaded areas, mountainous regions across Himalayan region, Indian Subcontinent.
Traditionally, it is used for Traditional respiratory support, joint health, rheumatic conditions and contains active compounds like Polysaccharides, mucilage, alkaloids, cardiac glycosides (trace).
Preferred cultivation conditions include Temperate-subtropical, 10-25°C, high humidity, 1500-3000mm rainfall and Well-drained loamy soil, shade-loving, forest soil.
Safety considerations: Generally safe.
Leaf features: Lanceolate, 5-8cm, glabrous, whorled arrangement (variable), margin entire.
Rauvolfia serpentina (6_22_sarpagandha) is a Perennial Shrub/Small tree in the Apocynaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical wet and dry forests, shaded forest areas across Indian Subcontinent.
Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic nervous system support, hypertension management, mental conditions and contains active compounds like Reserpine, ajmaline, serpentine, alstonine (alkaloids).
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical, 20-30°C, high humidity, 1500-2500mm rainfall, shade-loving and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, forest soil, slightly acidic.
Safety considerations: CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy; potentially teratogenic; avoid in lactation.
Leaf features: Lanceolate, 8-12cm, glabrous, whorled arrangement (3 per node), acuminate.
Hemidesmus indicus (6_23_anantamul) is a Perennial Herb (trailing, climber-like) in the Apocynaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical deciduous forests, open grasslands, cultivation across Indian Subcontinent, tropical Asia.
Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic blood purification, skin conditions, rheumatic support, cooling tonic and contains active compounds like Flavonoids, phenols, tannins, saponins, coumarins.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-32°C, moderate rainfall (1000-2000mm) and Well-drained sandy loam, adaptable, slightly acidic.
Safety considerations: Generally safe; traditionally used.
Leaf features: Lanceolate-elliptic, 2-4cm, glabrous, opposite arrangement, margin entire.
Artabotrys hexapetalus (6_24_chapalish) is a Perennial Shrub/Small tree in the Annonaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical evergreen forests, cultivated gardens across Indian Subcontinent, tropical Asia.
Traditionally, it is used for Traditional digestive aid, fever management, skin conditions and contains active compounds like Flavonoids, phenols, alkaloids, tannins.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical, 20-32°C, high humidity, 1500-2500mm rainfall and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, slightly acidic.
Safety considerations: Generally safe.
Leaf features: Elliptic-lanceolate, 8-15cm, glabrous, alternate arrangement, acuminate apex.
Phyllanthus emblica (6_25_amloki) is a Perennial Tree (medium) in the Phyllanthaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical deciduous forests, cultivated orchards across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic rejuvenative tonic, immune support, cooling, digestive aid (Triphala ingredient) and contains active compounds like Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), phyllemblic acid, emblicanin A & B, tannins.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-35°C, moderate rainfall (900-2250mm) and Well-drained loamy soil, slightly acidic to alkaline, fertile.
Safety considerations: Safe and beneficial in pregnancy and lactation; traditional rejuvenative.
Leaf features: Leaflets small, 0.4-0.8cm, pinnate feathery arrangement, light green.
Terminalia chebula (6_26_haritoki) is a Perennial (long-lived, 100+ years) Tree (large) in the Combretaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical deciduous and dry forests, cultivated across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic rasayana (rejuvenative), digestive aid, parasitic support, taste enhancer (Triphala ingredient) and contains active compounds like Tannins (30-35%), chebulic acid, ellagic acid, gallic acid, ascorbic acid.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 15-35°C, moderate rainfall (750-2250mm), drought tolerant and Well-drained loamy soil, adaptable, tolerates poor soils.
Safety considerations: Safe in pregnancy and lactation at normal medicinal doses; mild laxative action acceptable.
Leaf features: Elliptic, 8-15cm, glabrous, opposite to subopposite arrangement, leathery.
Terminalia bellirica (6_27_bohera) is a Perennial (long-lived, 100+ years) Tree (large) in the Combretaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical deciduous forests, cultivated across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic eye tonic, respiratory support, fever management, cooling (Triphala ingredient) and contains active compounds like Tannins (25-30%), belliric acid, polyphenols, vitamin C.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 15-35°C, moderate rainfall (750-2250mm) and Well-drained loamy soil, adaptable, tolerates poor soils.
Safety considerations: Safe in pregnancy and lactation at normal medicinal doses.
Leaf features: Obovate to elliptic, 10-20cm, glabrous, alternate to subopposite, leathery.
Withania somnifera (6_28_oshwagandha) is a Perennial Herb/Shrub in the Solanaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical dry forests, arid regions, cultivated across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Ayurvedic rasayana (rejuvenative), adaptogen, male fertility support, stress and sleep support and contains active compounds like Withanolides (7-60%, 40+ identified), alkaloids, phenols, tannins.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 15-35°C, drought tolerant, 400-1200mm rainfall and Well-drained sandy loam, drought tolerant, slightly alkaline.
Safety considerations: Generally regarded as safe but use with caution in pregnancy; acceptable in lactation.
Leaf features: Ovate to lanceolate, 3-8cm, pubescent, alternate arrangement, margin entire.
Euphorbia tithymaloides (6_29_devils_backbone) is a Perennial Herb/Succulent shrub in the Euphorbiaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical regions, cultivated ornamentally across Tropical Americas.
Traditionally, it is used for Limited traditional medicinal use; primarily ornamental and contains active compounds like Cardiac glycosides, alkaloids, phenols (potential toxins).
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-30°C, moderate to low rainfall, drought tolerant and Well-drained sandy loam, drought tolerant, poor soil adaptable.
Safety considerations: AVOID in pregnancy and lactation; cardiac glycoside toxicity risk.
Leaf features: Opposite, elliptic-obovate, 2-5cm, glabrous, margin entire, variegated in some varieties.
Cymbopogon citratus (7_30_lemongrass) is a Perennial Grass (tall perennial) in the Poaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical grasslands, cultivated widely across Tropical Asia, Southeast Asia.

Traditionally, it is used for Traditional digestive aid, fever management, insect repellent, calming tea and contains active compounds like Citral (geranial & neral, 70-80%), limonene, myrcene, linalool.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-30°C, moderate rainfall (750-2000mm), warm growing conditions and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral.
Safety considerations: Safe in pregnancy and lactation at normal culinary amounts.
Leaf features: Long, linear, 30-90cm, narrow (0.3-0.5cm wide), blade margins rough/serrulate, tufted.
Aloe vera (7_31_aloe_vera) is a Perennial Succulent herb in the Asphodelaceae family.
It naturally grows in Arid and semi-arid regions, xerophytic habitats across North Africa, Arabian Peninsula, naturalized in Mediterranean.

Traditionally, it is used for Traditional skin care, wound healing, digestive aid (caution), cooling, Ayurvedic pitta balance and contains active compounds like Polysaccharides (acemannan), mucilage, anthraquinones (aloin, barbaloin), salicylic acid.

Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 15-32°C, drought tolerant, low rainfall (250-1000mm), frost sensitive and Well-drained sandy soil, drought tolerant, poor soil adaptable.
Safety considerations: Gel safe topically in pregnancy; internal latex AVOID; gel juice minimal in lactation.
Leaf features: Lanceolate, succulent, 30-60cm long, blue-green, margin serrate with teeth, thick gel interior.
Catharanthus roseus (7_32_nayontara) is a Perennial Herb/Subshrub in the Apocynaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical deciduous forests, now cultivated widely across Madagascar.

Traditionally, it is used for Traditional folk remedy for diabetes, blood sugar management, cancer research (alkaloids) and contains active compounds like Indole alkaloids (vincristine, vinblastine, ajmalicine, serpentine).
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-32°C, moderate rainfall (800-1500mm) and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral.
Safety considerations: CONTRAINDICATED in pregnancy (cytotoxic alkaloids); AVOID in lactation.
Leaf features: Oblong-elliptic, 2-5cm, glabrous, opposite arrangement, margin entire, leathery.
Talinum triangulare (7_33_longevity_spinach_gainura) is a Perennial Herb/Succulent in the Talinaceae (formerly Portulacaceae) family.
It naturally grows in Tropical cultivated areas, open disturbed areas across Tropical Americas, now pan-tropical.

Traditionally, it is used for Traditional longevity tonic, blood building, nutritive support, energy enhancement and contains active compounds like Minerals (iron, calcium, potassium), vitamins (A, C), phytochemicals.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical-subtropical, 20-32°C, moderate rainfall (600-1500mm) and Well-drained sandy loam, adaptable, poor soil tolerant.
Safety considerations: Safe and beneficial in pregnancy and lactation; nutritive tonic.
Leaf features: Triangular to ovate, 2-5cm, glabrous, fleshy succulent, alternate arrangement.
Piper betle (7_34_betal) is a Perennial Vine (climber) in the Piperaceae family.
It naturally grows in Tropical wet forests, cultivated on support structures across Indian Subcontinent.

Traditionally, it is used for Traditional digestive stimulant, oral freshener, after-meal digestive aid, betel preparation and contains active compounds like Safrole, phenols, tannins, essential oils (betel oil), eugenol, anethole.
Preferred cultivation conditions include Tropical, 20-32°C, high humidity, 1500-2500mm rainfall, shade-loving and Well-drained loamy soil, fertile, high humidity required.
Safety considerations: Minimal concern at normal use; caution with excessive chewing in pregnancy.
Leaf features: Cordate (heart-shaped), 5-15cm long, acuminate, glabrous, alternate arrangement, aromatic.
